sentences.zh: ◎屬國表 周有天下，不期而會者八百餘國。

translations.literal: ◎ Vassal States Table. When Zhou possessed the empire, more than eight hundred states came to assemble without prior appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Vassal States Table. When the Zhou held sway over the realm, more than eight hundred states gathered of their own accord, unbidden.

translations.literal: The Liao dwelt in the Pine Desert and was the most powerful.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao, established in the Songmo steppe, stood supreme in strength.

translations.literal: Heaven's Mandate had its destination; they established the state and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven's Mandate found its fulfillment, they founded their state and inaugurated a new reign era.

translations.literal: Orders, laws, and regulations all followed Han institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Their edicts and legal institutions all followed the Han model.

translations.literal: They appointed generals to lead armies forth, and the various states submitted.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched generals on campaign until the various states submitted in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 人民皆入版籍，貢賦悉輸內帑。

translations.literal: The people all entered the household registers; tribute and levies all flowed into the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: All peoples were entered on the registers, and tribute and taxes were paid wholly into the imperial treasury.

translations.literal: East, west, north, and south—how could it be less than ten thousand li?
translations.idiomatic: From east to west and north to south, their sway stretched no less than ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 視古起百里國而致太平之業者，亦幾矣。

translations.literal: Compared with antiquity's kings who rose from hundred-li states to achieve the enterprise of Great Peace, they came close indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with ancient rulers who began with a state of a hundred li and brought about an age of Great Peace, they came very near indeed.

translations.literal: Therefore the grandeur of the Liao cannot go unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the splendor of Liao must be set down in writing.

translations.literal: The "Table of Vassal States" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the compilation of the Table of Vassal States.

cells.content: 遣耶律奴哥等使金國，復議和好。保安軍節度使張崇以雙州民二百戶歸金國。

cells.content: 金師至居庸關，耶律大石被擒。金師圍輜重於青塚硬寨。金遣人以書來招，回書請和。金帥以兵送族屬東行，乃遣兵邀戰於白水濼，為金師所敗。金帥以書來招，以書答之，金帥復書，不許請和。

translations.literal: The Jin army reached Juyong Pass; Yelü Dashi was captured. The Jin army besieged the baggage train at Green Mound Hard Stockade. Jin sent someone with a letter to summon surrender; Liao replied requesting peace. The Jin commander sent the imperial clan eastward with troops, then dispatched troops to intercept at White Water Marsh and was defeated by the Jin army. The Jin commander sent a letter summoning surrender; Liao replied in writing; the Jin commander wrote again, refusing the request for peace.
